stories.title: IOC books a record ₹22,503 crore profit as crude eases
stories.summary: Indian Oil Corporation reported a record September quarter profit of ₹22,503 crore, 2.7 times a year earlier, helped by lower crude between July and mid-August and strong petrochemical and gas margins. It lost ₹1,241 crore in the June quarter. It warns inventory losses may return if crude falls.

stories.title: IOC expects LPG under-recovery to reach ₹370 a cylinder in December
stories.summary: IOC's finance director Anuj Jain told analysts the under-recovery on a 14.2kg domestic LPG cylinder rose from ₹184 in September to ₹229 in October and should be about ₹309 in November and ₹370 in December. IOC's cumulative LPG under-recovery stood at ₹32,505.69 crore on 30 September.

stories.title: Muthoot Finance's profit rises 36 per cent on gold loans
stories.summary: Muthoot Finance reported Q2 FY27 consolidated profit after tax of ₹3,278 crore, up 36 per cent year on year. Total income rose 37 per cent to ₹10,011 crore, and consolidated loan assets under management grew 42 per cent to ₹2.09 trillion from ₹1.48 trillion. Gold remains a good business.

stories.title: IndiGo loses money for a third straight quarter and its shares rise 4 per cent
stories.summary: IndiGo posted a consolidated Q2 loss of ₹1,879.1 crore despite revenue growth of 26 per cent to ₹23,360 crore, its third straight quarterly loss. JM Financial had expected a ₹2,180 crore loss, so the shares rose 4 per cent to ₹4,868. Analysts still see a weak earnings outlook.

stories.title: Birla Corporation's profit falls 58.9 per cent as pet coke climbs 64 per cent
stories.summary: Birla Corporation's consolidated net profit fell to ₹37 crore in the September quarter from ₹90 crore, on higher input costs and weaker cement prices. Revenue grew 9 per cent to ₹2,441 crore. Power and fuel costs rose 15 per cent as pet coke jumped 64 per cent.

stories.title: Tilaknagar's volumes rise 160 per cent and its profit falls 57.7 per cent
stories.summary: Tilaknagar Industries reported Q2 net profit of ₹22.26 crore, down from ₹52.67 crore, after an exceptional loss of ₹10.94 crore from integrating Imperial Blue, bought from Pernod Ricard India. Volume grew 160 per cent to 8.9 million cases. Buying a big whisky brand turns out to cost money.

stories.title: GIC Re's profit falls 14.5 per cent as revenue rises 18 per cent
stories.summary: General Insurance Corporation of India reported Q2 FY27 revenue of ₹10,559.68 crore, up 18.31 per cent from ₹8,925.33 crore. Net profit fell 14.54 per cent to ₹2,455.62 crore from ₹2,873.54 crore. The results were declared on 30 October.

stories.title: Bank lending to the commercial sector jumps 55 per cent as bond issues dry up
stories.summary: Funding to India's commercial sector rose 55.4 per cent to ₹17.5 lakh crore in April to August FY27, the Finance Ministry's monthly review shows. Non-food bank credit was ₹9.8 lakh crore against ₹3.8 lakh crore a year earlier, while corporate bond issues fell to ₹0.3 lakh crore as yields rose.

stories.title: Banks see working capital demand rise 15 to 20 per cent on West Asia disruption
stories.summary: Working capital demand at Indian banks has risen 15 to 20 per cent over the past few months as raw material costs climb and shipping takes longer, The Economic Times reported, citing bankers. Refinancing, acquisitions and early signs of private capex revival have also lifted corporate borrowing.

stories.title: Government raises windfall tax on diesel exports and scraps it on petrol
stories.summary: The government has raised the export duty on diesel, with the special additional excise duty plus cess now ₹11.5 a litre from ₹8.5, and on ATF to ₹11 from ₹10.5. Duty on petrol exports drops to nil from ₹2.5 a litre. The rates apply for the fortnight from 31 October.

stories.title: Centre releases ₹1.09 lakh crore extra to states before the festive season
stories.summary: The Centre has released an additional tax devolution instalment of ₹1,09,019 crore to state governments, on top of regular monthly devolution, the finance ministry said. It is the second additional instalment this year, meant to help states speed up capital spending and fund development and welfare work.

stories.title: Centre forms a banking reform panel under Suresh N. Patel
stories.summary: The finance ministry has set up a high-level committee to recommend structural, regulatory and legislative reforms to make Indian banking globally competitive by 2047. Former central vigilance commissioner Suresh N. Patel chairs it, with RBI deputy governor Shirish Chandra Murmu, Padmaja Chunduru and N.S. Vishwanathan. It has six months.

stories.title: India to meet liquor makers as the Scotch dispute widens
stories.summary: India will hold talks with liquor companies on Monday after domestic firms joined Diageo and Pernod in protesting a probe into bulk Scotch imports, Reuters reports. New Delhi says bulk imports do not qualify for the India-UK pact's tariff cut to 75 per cent from 150 per cent.

stories.title: Households that shop online spend 7.5 per cent more, SBI Research finds
stories.summary: Households using online purchase or payment have 7.5 per cent higher monthly per capita consumption than non-adopters, SBI Research finds, with spending on services 23.4 per cent and durables 24.5 per cent higher. About 45.6 per cent of households use online purchase or payment for at least one item.

stories.title: Indian shares end a two-month losing run as IT surges 17.7 per cent
stories.summary: The Nifty rose 1.9 per cent and the Sensex 2.7 per cent in October, snapping two months of losses on IT stocks, earnings and hopes of a capital gains tax cut. The Nifty IT index jumped 17.7 per cent, its best month in over six years. Rising crude limited gains.

stories.title: BSE IT index heads for its second sharpest month in two decades
stories.summary: The BSE IT index had rallied 14.8 per cent in October by Friday, on course for its second sharpest monthly gain in over 20 years, behind July 2020's 22.6 per cent. Investors are betting on gradual growth improvement in FY28, with Infosys, Wipro and Coforge among the gainers.

stories.title: Sensex and Nifty rise 2 per cent in the week as Brent touches $114
stories.summary: Indian benchmarks rose about 2 per cent in the week to 30 October and the Nifty Smallcap 100 jumped 4 per cent, led by Trent, Upstox reports. Pharma and media indices gained 7.1 and 4.3 per cent. Brent crude climbed past $114 a barrel on West Asia worries.

stories.title: Wall Street dumps tech as AI bills come due
stories.summary: Tech stocks sold off on Wall Street this week as investors worried that heavy AI infrastructure spending will not lift profits fast enough, Mint reports. Cloud and AI kept growing, but data centre and chip costs drew the focus. The Nasdaq 100 fell 6.7 per cent in October.

stories.title: Gold drops ₹3,200 to a 10-month low in Delhi
stories.summary: Gold fell ₹3,200 to ₹1,42,000 per 10 grams in Delhi on Saturday, its lowest in 10 months, according to the All India Sarafa Association. Silver dropped ₹4,200 to ₹1,86,000 a kilogram. Traders cited rising energy prices fuelling inflation fears and hawkish US Fed commentary.

stories.title: CDSL's profit rises 24 per cent as 7.5 million demat accounts open
stories.summary: CDSL reported Q2 FY27 consolidated net profit of ₹173 crore, up 24 per cent, as 7.5 million demat accounts were added. Total income rose 22 per cent to ₹417 crore. Profit jumped 47 per cent from ₹118 crore in the June quarter.

stories.title: SEBI bars EKI Energy's MD for a year over misstated accounts
stories.summary: SEBI has barred carbon credit trader EKI Energy Services and its MD Manish Kumar Dabkara from the market for two months and 12 months for misrepresenting financial statements and diverting funds. Its former CFO is barred for eight months. Penalties total ₹88 lakh, and Dabkara must recoup the diverted money.

stories.title: SEBI to issue an FII compliance paper within weeks
stories.summary: SEBI chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey says a consultation paper on aligning foreign institutional investor norms with global standards will be released 'within weeks'. Foreign investors have pulled a net $31.4 billion from Indian equities this year. SEBI will also consult on capacity building for independent directors.

stories.title: Pandey says SEBI wants fundraising simpler and compliance cheaper
stories.summary: SEBI chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey told a Bharat Chamber of Commerce event that world-class markets need more than higher market cap and volumes, and must connect household savings with productive investment. 'Good businesses should be able to access suitable forms of capital through efficient and transparent processes,' he said.

stories.title: India's forex reserves slip $1.27 billion to $719.75 billion
stories.summary: India's foreign exchange reserves fell $1.27 billion to $719.75 billion in the latest reporting week as a $2.65 billion drop in gold holdings outweighed gains in foreign currency assets, RBI data show. Reserves peaked at $785.7 billion in early September and have declined since.

stories.title: Kotak's Sanjeev Prasad says India has two stock markets in one
stories.summary: Sanjeev Prasad of Kotak Institutional Equities discusses his recent reports with The Core, including one on large caps against mid and small caps titled Despair, Euphoria and Hope in the Same Market, and another on smaller IPOs giving higher returns. The full conversation is a long listen.

stories.title: PE and VC investment hits a 2026 high of $8 billion in October
stories.summary: Private equity and venture investments in India reached $8.02 billion in October, the highest month this year, Venture Intelligence data show. A single $5.6 billion bank deal made up about 70 per cent. Deal count fell to 106 from 125 in September. One cheque did most of the work.

stories.title: CCI clears the Devyani and Sapphire merger and Adani's IntelliSmart deal
stories.summary: The Competition Commission of India has approved five deals, including the merger of Sapphire Foods into Devyani International, which brings two big KFC and Pizza Hut operators together with over 3,000 stores. Approvals also cover Adani's ₹3,050 crore IntelliSmart deal, Aditya Birla Renewables, Prosus and Vodafone Group.

stories.title: CCI approves Xavier Niel's €5.1 billion Vodafone stake
stories.summary: The Competition Commission of India has approved French billionaire Xavier Niel's purchase of a 16.2 per cent stake in Vodafone Group from Emirates Telecommunications, a deal worth about €5.1 billion. Niel's Vega SAS has no direct operations in India but needed clearance, and will become Vodafone's largest shareholder.

stories.title: Marathon Nextgen buys Adani's stake in Mumbai's Monte South for ₹335 crore
stories.summary: Marathon Nextgen Realty will buy the Adani Group's 60 per cent stake in the Monte South mixed-use project at Byculla, Mumbai, for about ₹335 crore, taking full ownership. Monte South was the Adani Group's first premium Mumbai development. The group says it is focusing on larger projects in the region.

stories.title: TVS Capital Funds moves into private credit with a ₹750 crore fund
stories.summary: TVS Capital Funds has launched TVS Alts, a private credit platform targeting a ₹750 crore fund, with Shyam Srinivasan as co-founder and executive chairman. 'We are clear about looking at performing credit,' he said, focusing on firms with sound credit profiles and adequate security.

stories.title: Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Bank partners One Planet Partners on climate firms
stories.summary: India's One Planet Partners has formed a strategic partnership with Japan's Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Bank to provide growth capital to Indian mid-market climate-positive companies with revenue of ₹200 crore to ₹2,000 crore, in investments above ₹100 crore. Targets include fleet electrification and transmission equipment makers.

stories.title: Gufic pays ₹236 crore for a Juhu duplex with 10 parking spaces
stories.summary: Pharmaceutical company Gufic has bought a duplex in Lodha Developers' under-construction Avalon project in Juhu for ₹236.33 crore, property documents accessed by Zapkey show. The 14th-floor flat has 19,694 sq ft of carpet area, about ₹1.2 lakh per sq ft. That is a lot of parking.

stories.title: Landmark Group buys 22 acres on Dwarka Expressway
stories.summary: Landmark Group has acquired 22 acres on Dwarka Expressway for a planned ₹11,000 crore mixed-use and residential development, alongside its ₹4,000 crore Landmark One corporate project in Gurugram with 2.1 million sq ft of leasable space. Real estate veteran Pankaj Pal joins as managing director.

stories.title: NCLT cancels JLS Realty land transfer to Spenta and the ₹525 crore IIFL deal
stories.summary: The Mumbai bench of the NCLT has invalidated the transfer of a prime redevelopment plot from JLS Realty to Spenta Suncity and a mortgage and guarantee linked to ₹525 crore of IIFL financing. It also reversed share transfers and ordered the land restored, after five years of litigation.

stories.title: Carlyle and KKR line up to buy cheap US loans
stories.summary: Carlyle, KKR and Oaktree are among managers considering buying discounted US leveraged loans to package into collateralised loan obligations, Bloomberg reports. Barclays counts about 286 open warehouse lines for buying such loans, near a record. More than 90 per cent of loans trade at a discount.

stories.title: Apcotex buys a 1.275 per cent stake in a solar SPV for ₹72 lakh
stories.summary: Apcotex Industries has completed the purchase of 7,20,000 shares, or 1.275 per cent, of Amplus Ampere from NRB Bearings for ₹72 lakh in cash. Amplus Ampere is a power sector special purpose vehicle and subsidiary of Amplus Energy Solutions, according to the filing.

stories.title: Asian Granito pushes back its Sharjah subsidiary conversion to March
stories.summary: Asian Granito India says the conversion of a loan into equity in its Sharjah subsidiary Harmony Surfaces Marbles, about ₹3.38 crore for 372 shares, missed its 31 October deadline. It will now be completed on or before 31 March 2027, pending formalities.

stories.title: Why your October salary came in lower
stories.summary: Many salaried employees saw lower take-home pay in October because the mandatory EPF wage ceiling rose from ₹15,000 to ₹25,000 a month from 17 September, its first revision in 12 years. The impact depends on each salary structure, Mint explains. More savings, less to spend.

stories.title: GST changes from 1 November for online sellers
stories.summary: GST changes approved at the 57th GST Council meeting start from 1 November, covering registration, returns, refunds and post-sale discounts. Small sellers on e-commerce platforms will no longer need a physical office in every state where their goods are stored, the Times of India explains.

stories.title: How much RBI's new digital fraud rules will refund you
stories.summary: Under RBI rules from 1 January 2027, digital fraud victims can get compensation of up to 85 per cent of their net loss or ₹25,000, whichever is lower, Mint explains. The rules run for one year. RBI has also shifted the burden of proving customer liability in complaints.

stories.title: How EPFO invests your PF money, and why startups may join the list
stories.summary: EPFO is drafting guidelines to put 3 per cent of fresh annual investments into Category I and II alternative investment funds, including those that back startups, Mint explains. EPFO has traditionally stuck to government securities and debt. The proposal needs approval from its Central Board of Trustees.

stories.title: What the EPF withdrawal limits actually allow
stories.summary: EPFO members can withdraw up to 75 per cent of their provident fund balance, keeping at least 25 per cent as a buffer, under rules simplified last year, Mint explains. Thirteen partial withdrawal provisions were merged into essential needs, housing and special circumstances.

stories.title: Would a lower LTCG tax bring foreign investors back?
stories.summary: Foreign portfolio investors have pulled about ₹2.95 lakh crore from Indian equities in 2026, almost twice 2025's ₹1.66 lakh crore, Outlook Money notes. It explains long-term capital gains tax and asks if a cut would help, while a weak rupee, high valuations and global rates remain concerns.

stories.title: Money rules that change from 1 November
stories.summary: Several financial changes take effect from 1 November, Mint explains, including GST provisions, revised bank charges and the life certificate window for pensioners. Central government pensioners under 80 can submit certificates from 1 to 30 November, in person or through Jeevan Pramaan.

stories.title: Why longer payment terms hurt small exporters
stories.summary: A manufacturer exporting ₹1 crore a month and paid in 30 days would see receivables rise by ₹2 crore if payment terms stretch to 90 days. New markets can mean bigger clients and less cash. ADB put the global trade finance gap at $2.5 trillion in 2025.

stories.title: CBDT sets merger rules for charitable trusts
stories.summary: New CBDT rules notified on 30 October require non-profits merging with another registered organisation to inform the tax department, get accounts audited and state reasons. The surviving organisation cannot change objectives for five years, and the merger must not benefit specified related persons, The Economic Times explains.

stories.title: How India lifted 49.6 crore people out of poverty, by the World Bank's count
stories.summary: The World Bank's India Poverty and Equity Brief says the share of Indians below the $4.20 a day line fell from 57.7 per cent in 2011 to 16.1 per cent in 2023, lifting about 496 million people. Extreme poverty at $3 a day fell from 27.1 to 2.6 per cent.

stories.title: Where AI could save hospitals money
stories.summary: Revenue cycle management, from eligibility checks to coding and denial prediction, is where AI could cut hospital costs fastest, an Economic Times piece argues. IRDAI data for FY2024-25 show ₹1,32,488 crore in health claims, ₹94,248 crore paid. AI cannot legitimately remove contractual exclusions, the writer cautions.
